methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $1.7B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atoms, a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Travis Kalanick, has raised $1.7B to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 peers in Robotics & Manufacturing—1 public (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables to support a reliable median-multiple approach; only one methodologically defensible valuation technique applied.

The Stage-Progression method uses the $1.7B total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement, yielding $2.0B. This single-method triangulation produces a range bounded by $1.7B (floor, using raised capital directly) and $2.3B (ceiling, applying a more expansive interpretation of stage progression). The $2.0B median reflects typical post-growth venture outcomes in the sector.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.7B to $2.3B, centered near $2.0B, but relies on limited comparable data and a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include absence of narrowly comparable Growth-stage peers, lack of operational metrics to cross-check against revenue multiples, and sensitivity to assumed step-up multiples. Closer peer alignment and profitability trajectory would materially refine this estimate.
